title: reading-notes-llm-inference-nora-blake
content:
Quick reading notes + takeaways from recent papers and NeurIPS 2025 sessions (rapid scratchpad)

Context / why I care
- Trying to reduce 3-10% p99 latency on our hosted API without regressing output quality. Also thinking about Dedicated cost profiles (batching/quantization tradeoffs).
- These notes are for: proposal to runtime team, quick follow-ups for profiling experiments, and a couple of eval prompts to add to our regression harness.

Papers / tech highlights
1) FlashAttention follow-ups (sparse attention kernels + memory-friendly KV)
- Key idea: block-sparse / fused CUDA kernels to reduce memory movement for attention. Gains at long sequences (4k+).
- Practical: if we expect >2k tokens often, moving to fused kernels gives 15-30% mem bandwidth savings; can cascade into latency wins for decoder-only streaming workloads.
- Questions: compatibility with our quantized kernels? Need to check whether fused kernels assume FP16/FP32 conv; for int8 we'd need separate kernels or fall back.
- Action: add experiment: run 1k/2k/4k synthetic traces through runtime with flash-attention kernel enabled vs baseline (model: LLaMA-2-13B-CHAT variant)

2) Post-training quantization + outlier-aware schemes
- Outlier-aware quantization (detect and treat outlier weights separately) reduces perplexity hit vs naive 8-bit. There was a simple hybrid approach that keeps a small FP16 residue for outlier rows.
- Tradeoff: small memory increase (~1-2%) but big quality win on few-shot tasks.
- For Redwood Optimize: flag models with high outlier ratio and recommend OAwQ profile.
- Action: add a quantization diagnostic to model onboarding: histogram of weight magnitudes, outlier rows percent, expected quality delta estimate.

3) Sparse attention approximations for long-context retrieval pipelines
- Several groups showing locality-sensitive hashing + learnable sparsity patterns can reduce compute for long contexts when semantic retrieval returns many segments.
- Use-case fit: customers using retrieval-augmented generation with many retrieved chunks (10-50). We could route longer contexts to a sparse-attn variant to lower cost.
- Risk: unpredictable quality on complex compositional prompts. Need eval set.

4) Eval and benchmarking reproducibility (NeurIPS workshop takeaways)
- Reproducibility is still messy: differences in tokenizers, pre/post-processing, and sampling seeds cause nontrivial deltas in reported metrics.
- Recommendation for Redwood: publish a canonical eval harness (deterministic tokenization + seed) for model cards so customers can reproduce perf/quality.
- Note from talk: include the exact model weights tag + quantization profile + kernel versions in any benchmark artifact. Useful for our Model Catalog.

NeurIPS session notes (selected)
- Systems panel: latency SLOs are shifting to percentiles beyond p99 (p99.9 matters for high-traffic interactive apps). Techniques: prioritized retry/backpressure + small-batch fast path.
- Ops talk: automatic fallback to smaller model variants reduced outages during peak by 3x when paired with adaptive retry/backoff and memoized prompts. Relevant for our graceful degradation features.

Ideas / quick experiments to run
- Experiment A: kernel compatibility matrix
  - Run a small matrix: (FP16, INT8, OAwQ) x (baseline kernel, flash kernel, fused-sparse kernel) on the same 13B chat model. Measure 95/99/99.9 latencies, token/sec, and memory.
  - Instrument KV-cache eviction/scanning cost separately.

- Experiment B: quantization-on-deploy smoke test
  - For 5 customer-like prompt sets (chat, summarization, code), compare baseline vs int8 vs OAwQ under 1) interactive (single request) 2) batch (50 requests) workloads. Collect quality metrics (exact-match/code compile, ROUGE-like, and human eval proxy where possible).

- Experiment C: retrieval-heavy sparse-attn routing
  - Make a routing policy: if retrieved segments > N (sweep N in 4,8,16) then use sparse-attn variant. Measure end-to-end lat + downstream QA accuracy.

Notes-to-self / operational items
- Add kernel version + quant profile to model metadata (Model Catalog page). Helps debugging customer tickets where perf differs.
- Need a short README for SRE on how fallback to smaller model works (order of operations, token accounting, billing edge cases).
- Check with release-engineering: are any CUDA kernels pinned for specific driver versions in Dedicated? That's a likely mismatch vector.

Linked quick refs (from memory, verify links)
- FlashAttention repo and follow-ups: https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attention (check latest forks for fused-sparse)
- ArXiv: kernel optimizations and outlier-aware quantization papers (referenced above)

Loose ideas to prototype later
- Micro-batching scheduler that prefers low-latency fast-path for streams under 1k tokens and aggregates longer chat turns for batching. Could be a per-customer policy.
- Lightweight runtime shim to detect quantization drift: sample outputs on a small eval set post-deploy and compare to baseline distribution; auto-trigger rollback if drift > threshold.

Questions for team sync
- Runtime: feasibility of integrating fused attention kernels into our quantized execution path? Cost-to-implement estimate?
- Applied-ML: define a minimal quality diagnostic to decide OAwQ vs straight int8 (one metric we can compute cheaply).
- Product: do we expose a toggle for customers to prefer latency vs cost (and opt-in to fallback model routing)? How to show inferred cost savings in Console?

Next steps (my TODOs)
- Week 1: run Experiment A matrix on staging nodes (spin up nightly jobs) and share results with Evelyn.
- Week 2: sketch a Model Catalog metadata extension for kernel + quant profile to propose in product sync.
- Add these 5 prompts to the eval harness: short-chat, long-chat (2k), summarization (doc->summary), code-complete, retrieval-QA (multiple chunks).

End of notes.

-- Nora

(Informal — keep in Drive. Will turn into a short tech note if experiments show promising wins.)
